title: A dyadic vanishing remainder

blocks.text: The lacunary series f(x) = Σ x^(2^n), where 2^n means 2 raised to n, obeys f(x) = x + f(x²). Along the specified dyadic path toward 1, subtracting k and a convergent constant leaves an explicit tail.

blocks.label: Proved pathwise bound
blocks.text: The proof concerns x_k = exp(−2^(−k)). Its additive constant belongs to that path; the arithmetic classification of f(exp(−1)) is a separate question.

An index shift and elementary exponential bounds give the dyadic argument. A later companion proof establishes R_k/(ζ(k) − 1) → 1 as integer k → ∞; it is an asymptotic comparison of two separately defined sequences.
Quantify the finite-k relative error beyond the proved leading-ratio limit, or define a structural map and the property it preserves. A shared dynamical system or conjugacy remains open.

blocks.label: Scope of the limit
blocks.text: Along x_k = exp(−2^(−k)), the remainder bound gives f(x_k) = k + C + O(2^(−k)). The constant C belongs to this specified path. The arithmetic classification of f(exp(−1)) remains a separate question.
The input exp(−1) is transcendental. A Mahler-value theorem requiring algebraic input therefore needs different hypotheses before it can apply here.
